question: With oracle-verified local-progress actions available, what changes when Director messages are removed, and can a no-message oracle policy complete the tasks?

source.adapter: v0.23 recent-16-line history, parser, failed-call omission, UTF-8, distinct Director scheduling where applicable

model.runtime: llama.cpp b11202; 99 GPU layers; one slot; context 4096; batch 1024; micro-batch 256; Director temperature 0.7/max_tokens 500; Builder temperature 0.1/max_tokens 250

conditions.name: zero_message_random_oracle_policy
conditions.candidate_policy: uniform random from candidates using a separate fixed RNG

design.initialization: Upstream partComplete=True; record exact realized starting board and partialCompletionCategory per structure.

primary_outcomes: per-turn progress delta, executed move, oracle adherence, candidate count, and failed/clarification action
messages attempted, successfully parsed, delivered, and Builder-visible wire tokens
model calls, prompt/completion tokens, and service timing
analysis: Descriptive paired comparison across the same three structures and one seed. A completed oracle-policy episode falsifies strict communication necessity for that instance under this oracle. A failed oracle policy does not establish necessity. A zero-message LLM result estimates message removal under the given model, prompt, and oracle, not protocol superiority. No superiority, generalization, scaling, or frontier claim.
prediction: The random oracle policy makes local progress but may not complete within 20 turns because local progress is not globally optimal. If it completes, revise the benchmark's communication-necessity claim. If it fails, strengthen no-message policies and repeat paired seeds before asserting necessity.
